tasks.gr8-careers-and-career-choices-t4: Topic: Careers and career choices. Cover interests, abilities, occupations, work roles, and aspiration mapping. Ask Grade 8 learners to link strengths to possible pathways, compare career fields, and make informed early planning choices.
tasks.gr8-learning-styles-and-exam-readiness-t: Topic: Learning styles and exam readiness. Cover revision planning, memory strategies, note-making, time management, and stress management. Ask Grade 8 learners to select effective study routines, evaluate preparation habits, and choose calm test-readiness actions.
tasks.gr8-responsible-decision-making-t4: Topic: Responsible decision-making. Cover goals, consequences, influence, resilience, and healthy routines. Ask Grade 8 learners to apply structured decision steps in scenarios about schoolwork, friendships, and future planning.
tasks.gr8-physical-education-task-t4: Topic: Physical Education Task. Cover games application, personal fitness review, participation, recreation, and improvement tracking. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify effective movement choices, fair play, and ways to evaluate personal progress.
tasks.gr8-human-rights-violations-t4: Topic: Human rights violations and counter-strategies (Grade 8 Life Orientation, Term 4). Cover the Bill of Rights, what a violation is, types (discrimination, xenophobia, violence and abuse, child labour, denial of education), and peaceful lawful counter-strategies (speaking out, reporting, South African Human Rights Commission, courts, peaceful protest). Ask the learner directly (you).
tasks.gr8-gender-equity-and-gbv-t4: Topic: Gender equity and gender-based violence (Grade 8 Life Orientation, Term 4). Cover gender equity including in sport, stereotypes, what gender-based violence is, its emotional, health and social impact, the law on sexual offences at a general level, and sources of help: GBV Command Centre 0800 428 428, Childline 116, police 10111, clinic, teacher, social worker. No graphic scenarios; the victim is never blamed ('it is never your fault'). Ask the learner directly (you).
